title: Affine numerical cover and fixed coordinate polynomial of curve isomorphism graphs
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-pc-scheme], and let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be flat, finitely presented projective morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-kun-projective] with geometric fibres of dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Fix projective embeddings $i_X:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^a_S$ and $i_Y:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^b_S$, and let $L=i_X^*\mathcal O(1)$, $N=i_Y^*\mathcal O(1)$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-projective-space-twist]. There is an affine open cover $(U_i)$ of $S$ by Noetherian schemes such that the following hold on each $U=U_i$. The restrictions $X_U,Y_U$ are proper, flat and finitely presented [def-weil-proper-morphism]. There are integers $c_X,\lambda_X,c_Y,\lambda_Y$ such that for every field-valued point $t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to U$,
$$\chi(X_t,\mathcal O_{X_t})=c_X,\quad\chi(X_t,L_t)=\lambda_X,\quad\chi(Y_t,\mathcal O_{Y_t})=c_Y,\quad\chi(Y_t,N_t)=\lambda_Y$$
[def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Set $d_X=\lambda_X-c_X$, $d_Y=\lambda_Y-c_Y$, $P_X(n)=nd_X+c_X$, $P_Y(n)=nd_Y+c_Y$. For all $n\ge0$ these polynomials equal $\chi(X_t,L_t^{\otimes n})$ and $\chi(Y_t,N_t^{\otimes n})$. There is a closed immersion $j:E=X_U\times_UY_U\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{(a+1)(b+1)-1}_U$ whose pulled-back degree-one module is $M=\operatorname{pr}_X^*L\otimes\operatorname{pr}_Y^*N$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$, every $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, and every isomorphism $f:X_t\simeq Y_t$, its closed graph $\Gamma_f\subset E_t$ satisfies
$$\chi(\Gamma_f,M_t^{\otimes n}|_{\Gamma_f})=R(n)=n(d_X+d_Y)+c_X=P_X(n)+P_Y(n)-P_Y(0)\qquad(n\ge0).$$
Moreover $R$ is its coordinate Hilbert polynomial for $j_t$: for every homogeneous ideal defining $j_t(\Gamma_f)$, the dimension over $\Omega$ of its degree-$n$ coordinate quotient equals $R(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$ [def-sfb-projective-coordinate-hilbert-polynomial]. If such an $f$ exists then $c_X=c_Y$. Empty fibres have Euler characteristic and polynomial zero; no reducedness, pure dimension, connectedness or nonemptiness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the projective-twist data lemma to both specified embeddings. It gives properness of $X/S,Y/S$ and finite presentation and base-flatness of $\mathcal O_X,L,\mathcal O_Y,N$ (twists zero and one). Properness includes separatedness. Apply the graph-family base-change lemma with source $X$, target $Y$, and again with the roles reversed. In particular all restrictions to base opens and all field fibres are proper, flat and finitely presented, with separated targets. The induced twists are the pullbacks specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0D1A (lemma-Mor-into-Hilb), base-change paragraph; constructions.tex Tag 01MT (lemma-apply-modules), twists; morphisms.tex Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper).

proof.text: Apply Euler local constancy to the four modules of step 1. At each $s\in S$ intersect their four constancy neighbourhoods. Refine this open by affine opens contained in a Noetherian affine neighbourhood of $s$ from local Noetherianity. Such opens are Noetherian by the open-subscheme lemma. They give the required cover. On each $U$ call the four values $c_X,\lambda_X,c_Y,\lambda_Y$. The arbitrary-base-change clause of Euler local constancy, applied to $\operatorname{Spec}K\to U$, gives exactly these values at every field-valued point, not only at residue-field points.

We check the dimension hypothesis on all field fibres. Fix $s\in S$ and write $C=X_s$ or $Y_s$. If $C$ is empty, every scalar extension is empty. Otherwise the affine-cover scalar-extension lemma supplies matching affine covers $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_{\kappa(s)}F)$ for every field extension $F/\kappa(s)$; each $A_i$ is of finite type and the scalar extension is nonempty. Ring dimension is unchanged by field extension. The affine-open-cover dimension formula, together with the equality of scheme topological dimension and the supremum of its local-ring dimensions, therefore shows that $C_F$, $C$, and $C_{\overline{\kappa(s)}}$ have the same dimension. The last is at most one by hypothesis. Every field-valued fibre over $s$ is such a $C_F$, so the degree-additivity theorem applies to it.

source.place: Tag 00P3 (lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension); properties.tex Tag 04MU (lemma-dimension); matching scalar-extension affine charts as in the cited affine-cover node.

proof.text: For any proper field fibre $C$ and invertible module $A$, degree is $\chi(C,A)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$. In particular $\deg(\mathcal O_C)=0$. Tensor degree additivity and induction on $n$ give $\deg(A^{\otimes n})=n\deg(A)$: the case $n=0$ is the preceding identity, and the successor case adds $\deg(A)$. Thus $\chi(C,A^{\otimes n})=n\deg(A)+\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$ for every $n\ge0$. Applying this to $L_t,N_t$ using steps 2 and 3 gives exactly $P_X(n)=nd_X+c_X$ and $P_Y(n)=nd_Y+c_Y$. On an empty fibre all cohomology vector spaces are zero, so this argument also gives the asserted zero polynomial.

source.place: Tag 0AYR (definition-degree-invertible-sheaf) and Tag 0AYX (lemma-degree-tensor-product), rank-one case and induction.

proof.text: The product of the two base-changed embeddings is a closed immersion $E\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^a_U\times_U\mathbf P^b_U$ by the product clause of the closed-immersion permanence lemma; equivalently, it factors into two base changes of closed immersions, and a composite of closed immersions is a closed immersion by the same lemma. Compose with the Segre closed immersion to obtain $j$ into $\mathbf P^{(a+1)(b+1)-1}_U$. For the Segre coordinates $z_{rs}=x_ry_s$, the transition ratio of the pulled-back degree-one generator is $(x_ry_s)/(x_{r'}y_{s'})=(x_r/x_{r'})(y_s/y_{s'})$. This is precisely the product of the transition ratios of the two degree-one modules. After pulling back to $E$, these local identifications glue to $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*L\otimes\operatorname{pr}_Y^*N=M$.

source.place: Tag 01WD (lemma-segre-embedding), construction by the sections $X_iY_j$; schemes.tex Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion); morphisms.tex Tag 01QO (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Fix $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ and $f:X_t\simeq Y_t$. The graph-family lemma makes $(\mathrm{id},f)$ a closed immersion; its first projection is an isomorphism $\Gamma_f\simeq X_t$. Pullback preserves tensor products and their powers, so the restriction of $M_t^{\otimes n}$ to the graph identifies with $(L_t\otimes f^*N_t)^{\otimes n}$ on $X_t$. A scheme isomorphism identifies the sheaf categories by exact inverse functors and identifies global sections; applying these functors to an injective resolution identifies all cohomology groups. Consequently $\chi(X_t,\mathcal O)=\chi(Y_t,\mathcal O)$ and $\chi(X_t,f^*N_t)=\chi(Y_t,N_t)$; hence $c_X=c_Y$ and $\deg(f^*N_t)=d_Y$. By step 4 and degree additivity the graph Euler characteristic is $n(d_X+d_Y)+c_X$. Finally $P_X(n)+P_Y(n)-P_Y(0)=nd_X+c_X+nd_Y+c_Y-c_Y=R(n)$.

source.place: Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), displayed graph Euler calculation; varieties.tex Tags 0AYR and 0AYX; quot.tex Tag 0D1A (lemma-Mor-into-Hilb).

proof.text: Base change preserves the closed immersion $j$, and the composite of $j_t$ with the graph closed immersion is a closed immersion by the composite clause of the closed-immersion permanence lemma. Let $J$ be any homogeneous ideal defining this embedded graph. Apply the coordinate-ring/Euler comparison to $\Omega[z_0,\ldots,z_{(a+1)(b+1)-1}]/J$. For all sufficiently large $n$ its degree-$n$ dimension equals the Euler characteristic of its $n$th twist. That twist is $M_t^{\otimes n}|_{\Gamma_f}$: the transition rule $e_r^{(n)}=(z_r/z_{r'})^ne_{r'}^{(n)}$ of the twisting modules gives $\mathcal O(n)\cong\mathcal O(1)^{\otimes n}$ on $\mathbf P^{(a+1)(b+1)-1}_U$ and shows that the pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ along $\mathbf P^{(a+1)(b+1)-1}_\Omega\to\mathbf P^{(a+1)(b+1)-1}_U$ is $\mathcal O(1)$; the pullback and iterated-pullback compatibilities with tensor products then carry the identification $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong M$ of step 5 to $(j_t\circ\Gamma)^*\mathcal O(n)\cong M_t^{\otimes n}|_{\Gamma_f}$; step 6 identifies its Euler characteristic with $R(n)$. This proves the coordinate Hilbert-polynomial assertion for every such $J$, including nonsaturated ideals. The comparison explicitly allows the empty closed subscheme, for which the eventual dimensions and the polynomial vanish.
